claims.statement: FeedUrlValidatorTest verifies the SSRF guard in FeedUrlValidator by stubbing its package-private HostResolver to a fixed literal IP (avoiding real DNS), asserting public hosts are allowed while loopback, RFC1918 private, link-local/metadata (169.254.169.254), IPv6 unique-local (fc00::/7), CGNAT (100.64.0.0/10), broadcast, and IPv4-mapped-loopback addresses are rejected with a 'non-public' IllegalArgumentException, and that non-http(s) schemes and malformed URLs are rejected separately.

FeedFetcherTest exercises FeedFetcher against a MockRestServiceServer-backed RestClient, using a FeedUrlValidator stub that resolves every test host to a public IP so the SSRF guard doesn't block fixture requests; it covers raw-byte-plus-charset retrieval, conditional If-None-Match/If-Modified-Since requests mapping a 304 response to FetchResult.notModified(), ETag/Last-Modified header capture, FeedFetchException on HTTP error statuses, and rejection of a response body exceeding a configured byte cap via a package-private constructor overload.

ArticleExtractionServiceTest covers the reader-view extraction flow in ArticleExtractionService: caching behavior (extract-and-save via FeedFetcher plus Readability4J on first request, serving cached HTML without re-fetching on repeat requests, verified via verifyNoInteractions(feedFetcher)), NotFoundException (404) for a missing article, IllegalArgumentException (400) for an article with no URL, and mapping a page with no extractable content to FeedParseException (422).

ArticleExtractionService fetches an article's original page through FeedFetcher (preserving the SSRF guard, size cap, and User-Agent), decodes it with Jsoup using header-declared charset or Jsoup's own BOM/meta-tag detection, and extracts readable content via Readability4J, caching the extracted HTML through ArticleRepository so subsequent requests skip the fetch/parse step.

ArticleControllerTest includes WebMvcTest slice tests for GET /api/articles/{id}/extracted-content that assert the ArticleExtractionService result is returned as 200 with title/contentHtml JSON, a NotFoundException from the service maps to HTTP 404, and a FeedFetchException maps to HTTP 422.

HttpClientConfigurationTest guards the spring.http.clients.* connect-timeout/read-timeout configuration introduced with the Boot 4.0.8 upgrade by running an ApplicationContextRunner with only HttpClientAutoConfiguration/ImperativeHttpClientAutoConfiguration loaded (no Docker), asserting the auto-configured ClientHttpRequestFactory is a ReactorClientHttpRequestFactory, and loading src/main/resources/application.yaml from disk (since src/test/resources/application.yaml shadows it on the test classpath) to assert the bound HttpClientSettings connect/read timeouts equal the configured 5s/30s.

MockRestServiceServer-based backend tests such as FeedFetcherTest and the Raindrop client tests replace the outbound HTTP request factory entirely, so they cannot catch a regression in the real Reactor Netty transport or in the spring.http.clients.* timeout wiring; HttpClientConfigurationTest exists specifically to cover that gap.
